# Retry internal GitHub commit_refs_rules failures separately from repository rules

The JavaScript downstream release at https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42060440016 failed on 2026-11-05 at 16:03:47 UTC after creating its version commit:

```text
remote: fatal error in commit_refs_rules
! [remote rejected] HEAD -> main (fatal error in commit_refs_rules)
```

Inspection of this template's `scripts/version_and_commit.py` shows the same classification gap. `classify_push_failure` returns `PushFailure.OTHER` for this string, so `push_branch_with_rebase_retry` aborts instead of allowing a bounded retry of the unchanged commit. No Python template production failure is claimed; this is a reproducible shared helper defect exposed by downstream evidence.

Minimal reproduction:

```python
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, 'scripts')
from version_and_commit import classify_push_failure, PushFailure
result = classify_push_failure('remote: fatal error in commit_refs_rules')
assert result == PushFailure.OTHER  # demonstrates the missing transient class
```

To test recovery, mock `run_git_capturing` to return a `CompletedProcess` with return code 1 and this stderr, followed by a success. Assert identical push arguments, no rebase, and two calls. Also test three failures and GH013 combined with the internal-error text.

Workaround: inspect the remote commit and registry/release state before rerunning the release. Do not force push, bypass repository rules, or republish a version that already exists.

Suggested fix: introduce a transient classification for this exact internal GitHub failure and explicit HTTP 429/5xx errors; use at most three unchanged push attempts with backoff. Keep GH006/GH013 policy errors permanent, preserve stderr, and add default-off attempt/classification diagnostics. GitHub's internal trigger is unknown; an empty downstream rules API response is not proof that rules evaluation was disabled.

Analysis and bounded JavaScript regression tests are being implemented in https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/pull/93.
title: Classify internal commit_refs_rules push errors as bounded transient failures

body:
Found at `317c243a7cc832b0abfe4d30989c5095d17fcd78`, `scripts/create_github_release.py:79-108`, while auditing https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/pull/55. The section scanner treats Markdown headings inside fenced example code as real release boundaries, silently deleting the rest of the notes.

Minimal CHANGELOG.md:

````markdown
## 1.2.3

Example:

```md
## 9.9.9
```

Remaining details.

## 1.2.2
old
````

Expected: the 1.2.3 body contains the whole fenced example and `Remaining details.`. Actual: the body ends at `Example:` and the opening fence, leaving invalid Markdown and dropping real release information. A requested version that appears only inside a fenced example can also select example text as release notes.

Reproduce from the template root (no real publishing):

```sh
python3 -B <<'PY'
import sys, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0, 'scripts')
from create_github_release import extract_changelog_entry
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / 'CHANGELOG.md'
    path.write_text('## 1.2.3\n\nExample:\n\n```md\n## 9.9.9\n```\n\nRemaining details.\n\n## 1.2.2\nold')
    print(repr(extract_changelog_entry(path, '1.2.3')))
PY
```

The JS and Python snapshot functions were executed offline and both returned the truncated body. The Rust source has the same boundary error in `next_section_re`, which matches `^## [` without fence state; the above CLI reproduction uses a local gh stub. No Rust template build was run on the constrained downstream machine.

Workaround: use indented example code or avoid version-shaped headings inside fenced changelog examples until the scanner is fixed. Do not silently delete the example or the later prose from the actual release.

Suggested fix: find exact release headings only outside Markdown code fences (both backticks and tildes, matching closing delimiter/length), or parse Markdown to an AST and slice by top-level heading offsets. Preserve body bytes/indentation, fail explicitly on missing required entries, and add tests for a fenced next-version heading, a target version only inside a fence, CRLF and multiple change subsections. The downstream PR adds these regressions in `js/tests/ci-github-release.test.js` and fixes its shared release-content helper; the Rust/Python publication programs are template-specific and are not vendored into the product.
title: Release changelog extraction treats version headings inside fenced examples as release boundaries

body:
The template uses `actions/download-artifact@v8` with its default ZIP extraction. The current v8.0.2 bundle calls deprecated Buffer constructors through `unzip-stream`, producing DEP0005 on Node 24. This is the same issue reproduced in downstream Data.Doublets: https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/actions/runs/40917637619 and investigated in https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/pull/542.

Reproduce with an ordinary artifact round trip:

```yaml
- run: printf 'check\n' > check.txt
- uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
  with:
    name: check
    path: check.txt
- uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
  with:
    name: check
    path: downloaded
```

The download emits `[DEP0005] DeprecationWarning: Buffer() is deprecated`. A bounded offline reproduction and its stack trace are provided in the downstream PR (`experiments/reproduce_artifact_buffer.mjs`); it needs only two bytes and no credentials.

Workaround: use `skip-decompress: true` with digest verification left enabled, then extract with a maintained ZIP component such as Python `zipfile`, validating paths and symlinks first. Verify bytes with an upload/download regression on pull requests. Once an upstream release incorporates the fix, prefer that release and remove the workaround.

Upstream root cause and suggested code changes are tracked at https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/issues/484 and https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/pull/490: replace obsolete Buffer constructors throughout the transitive extraction dependencies, rebuild `dist/`, and test extraction with `NODE_OPTIONS=--throw-deprecation`. Pin reviewed action revisions so the behavior is reproducible.
title: Artifact downloads emit DEP0005 through the v8 ZIP extractor

body:
## Summary

The Python pipeline template's manual release passes a bump *type* to
`scriv collect --version` before it calculates the new package version:

```yaml
scriv collect --version "$BUMP_TYPE"
```

For a `patch` dispatch, Scriv therefore creates a changelog heading named
`patch`, consumes the fragments, and only afterwards
`scripts/version_and_commit.py` calculates the real numeric version. The
release script then cannot find that numeric version in `CHANGELOG.md` and
falls back to generic release notes.

Affected current template commit: `03f3c8475dd9e59327422b3e0b9971772820f115`.

## Reproducible example

```bash
git clone https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template
cd python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template
python -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
pip install 'scriv[toml]'
mkdir -p changelog.d
printf '### Fixed\n\n- Reproduction.\n' > changelog.d/repro.fixed.md
scriv collect --version patch
grep '^## ' CHANGELOG.md
```

Observed: the new heading is `## patch`, and the fragment is deleted.

Expected: the heading is the numeric version which the following
`version_and_commit.py --bump-type patch` command publishes.

This is also reproducible without a clone in Browser Commander CI history:
the downstream wrapper's regression test documents that the same call used to
write a section literally titled `patch`.

## Workaround

Compute the numeric next version first and pass that exact value to Scriv. If
the workflow has already consumed fragments into `## patch`, restore them from
Git and delete the invalid heading before retrying.

## Suggested code fix

Make versioning and changelog collection one atomic operation in
`scripts/version_and_commit.py`:

1. Run `bump_version.py`.
2. Re-read `project.version` as `new_version`.
3. If fragments exist, run `scriv collect --version new_version`.
4. Commit the version, fragments, and `CHANGELOG.md` together.

Then remove the workflow's earlier `Collect changelog fragments` step. Add a
test starting at `0.1.0`, dispatching `patch`, and asserting that the resulting
heading is `0.1.1`, never `patch`, and that release-note extraction finds the
fragment under `0.1.1`.

## Discovery context

Found while auditing every false positive, false negative, warning, and error
for link-foundation/browser-commander#99 / PR #100 and comparing all current
language template files.
title: Manual release writes changelog heading `patch`/`minor`/`major` instead of the released version
